issues.text: Run 1: wire the 5 devices as a daisy chain, one after another. Star and T connections are not allowed.
M1XIN (address 14): M1XIN hardwired input expander addresses run from 2 to 13.
Address 4 is used by 2 Type 1 devices: Keypad (address 4), M1KAM (address 4). Within a type every address must be different (a keypad and an M1XIN may share one, a keypad and an M1KAM may not).
The primary M1XRFTWM transceiver must be at address 2; the additional ones use 3, 4 and 5.
With wireless in use, each hardwired expander at address 3 to 10 (zones 33-160) uses up one group of 16 wireless zones. 0 of those here: at most 144 wireless zones remain (up to 144 without any).
No device currents entered, so the power load was not checked. The +12V keypad output of the control is protected at 1.25 A; the hub adds 30 mA, plus 20 mA per branch for the M1DBHR.
A data bus hub is the preferred way to wire a bus with several devices (new wiring: M1DBH with CAT5/6 home runs; reusing 4-conductor cable: M1DBHR). A direct bus is limited to two runs.

checklist.title: Control
items: JP3 (terminating jumper on the M1 control): INSTALL it. With one run, the control end is the second of the two termination points.
The data bus must have exactly two terminating points in total, never more.

checklist.title: Run 1
items: Daisy chain: control → Keypad (address 4) → M1KAM (address 4) → M1XIN (address 14) → M1XRFTWM (address 3) → Bogus "Q" (address 1). About 50 ft.
Terminate the last device only: Bogus "Q" (address 1). Fit its terminating jumper. Do not terminate the others.

checklist.title: Addresses to set
items: M1XRFTWM (address 3): additional transceiver; S1 on, S2 off, S3 off, S4 off
After setting the addresses, run Bus Module Enrollment (installer programming, or Live > Modules in this editor). Devices added later must be enrolled too.
